$comment: The code freeze register. H-MIG-11.
It ships LIVE AND OPEN rather than absent, which is the findings register's own argument (ADR
0125): a register created on the day somebody needs it is a register nobody has read, and a
missing one is indistinguishable from a tree nobody froze.
NOTHING IN THIS BUILD DECLARES A FREEZE. `state` is a value a person sets, in a commit somebody
reviews, together with the F07 ROLE that set it, the instant and the reason. There is no date
arithmetic, no 'frozen once the go/no-go passes' and no job that writes here: the cutover date is
not on file (OPEN-QUESTIONS Y13-cutover-date), so a mechanism that decided when to freeze would be
deciding a date this build invented (brief rule 15). This is the shape migration 0128 uses for
'Marked as posted', H-HARD-07's incident register for a declaration and 0153's
parallel_run_decision for the cutover decision.
`scripts/freeze.mjs --register-only` (`pnpm freeze`, a step of `pnpm verify`) refuses a frozen
register that names no role, no instant or no reason, refuses a claimant that is not an F07 role,
and refuses an open register that still carries a claim or names no open question. The merge rule
is the other entry point: `.github/workflows/freeze.yml` runs it on every pull request with that
request's labels, and while the tree is frozen a change is merged only if it is labelled
launch-blocking. That label is a constant in packages/core/src/release/freeze.ts and deliberately
not a field here: a label named in this file could be edited to one every pull request already
carries, and the freeze would then permit everything while reading as enforced.
To declare a freeze: set state to "frozen" and fill in claim with your role, the instant and why.
